label: Polish 'your' locative, activity type
summary: Text helper for the Polish translation: the activity type's name with 'your', in the locative case, without a tooltip.
details: It looks up the text named by the activity type's key plus `_your_locative` and gives that text. If no such text exists (the lookup only gives back the key itself), it gives just the Polish word 'twoim ' instead. Reading this from the macro; the game does not describe it further.

fields.name: ActivityType
fields.text: The activity type whose name is wanted.

label: Polish 'your', activity type
summary: Text helper for the Polish translation: the activity type's name with 'your' in front, without a tooltip.
details: It looks up the text named by the activity type's key plus `_your` and gives that text. If no such text exists (the lookup only gives back the key itself), it gives just the Polish word 'twój ' instead. Reading this from the macro; the game does not describe it further.

fields.name: ActivityType
fields.text: The activity type whose name is wanted.

label: Previous scope
summary: Going by its name, the thing the script was working on one step back, as a text sees it.
details: Vanilla uses it a few times to reach a character from it, for example "All dynasty members of [PREV's character]" and a debug log line that names THIS as the cheater and PREV as the partner. The game documents it only as a script scope.

label: Province
summary: The province a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in over 450 lines, for example where an epidemic began or where the AI's units support the player.

label: Puppet action
summary: The puppet action (something a character may do through a puppet) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's condition texts use it: "has a puppet that allows: ...", written for a given character.

label: Puppet type
summary: Gives a puppet type; the game documents only the return type.
details: Going by its name and return type, it stands for a puppet type. No use is shown.

label: Paradox account
summary: Gives a Paradox account object; the game documents only the return type.
details: Going by its name and return type, it stands for the Paradox account. No use is shown.

label: Clear edit box text
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, clears the text of an edit box.
details: It takes one argument, presumably the edit box. No use is shown.

label: Profiler names
summary: A developer function of the game's profiler; the game documents nothing more.
details: Its return type is listed as unregistered, so the game does not describe what it gives back.

label: Widget screen size
summary: Going by its name, gives the size of a GUI widget on the screen, as a pair of numbers.
details: Vanilla passes it to the portrait functions of a character, with `PdxGuiWidget.Self` (the widget itself) as the argument, so the portrait is made for the size of the widget that shows it.

label: Destroy widget
summary: A GUI command that destroys a widget.
details: The game documents it as 'Destroy widget' and takes one argument, presumably the widget. No use is shown.

label: Editor message box
summary: A GUI command that shows a message box.
details: The game documents it only as 'Message box'. The name suggests it belongs to the GUI editor. No use is shown.

label: Interrupt animations
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, stops all running animations with the given name.
details: Vanilla uses it in `on_start` of the main menu with names like 'main_menu_glow_exit_leave'. The meaning rests on the name and these uses.

label: Interrupt, then start animations
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, stops running animations of one name and then starts those of another.
details: Vanilla calls it in `onclick` with the same name twice (e.g. 'bookmark_change','bookmark_change'); going by the name, that restarts the animation. The meaning rests on the name and these uses.

label: Start animations
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, starts all animations with the given name.
details: Vanilla uses it in `on_start`, `on_finish` and `onclick` of widgets, e.g. 'bookmarks_bars_appear'. The meaning rests on the name and these uses.

label: Profiler filter next
summary: A developer command of the game's profiler; going by its name, it moves to the next filter.
details: The game documents nothing more. No use is shown.

label: Profiler filter previous
summary: A developer command of the game's profiler; going by its name, it moves to the previous filter.
details: The game documents nothing more. No use is shown.

label: Profiler filter timers
summary: A developer command of the game's profiler; going by its name, it filters the shown timers.
details: The game documents nothing more. No use is shown.

label: Profiler current frame
summary: A developer function of the game's profiler; going by its name, it gives the number of the current frame.
details: It returns a whole number. No use is shown.

label: Profiler frame time
summary: A developer function of the game's profiler; going by its name, it gives the frame time in milliseconds.
details: It returns a decimal number. No use is shown.

label: Profiler ns per tick
summary: A developer function of the game's profiler; going by its name, it gives how many nanoseconds one profiler tick lasts.
details: It returns a decimal number. No use is shown.

label: Profiler graph lines shown
summary: A developer function of the game's profiler; going by its name, it tells whether the graph lines are switched on.
details: It returns yes or no. No use is shown.

label: Toggle profiler graph lines
summary: A developer command of the game's profiler; going by its name, it switches the graph lines on or off.
details: The game documents nothing more. No use is shown.

label: Toggle profiler stats
summary: A developer command of the game's profiler; going by its name, it shows or hides the statistics.
details: The game documents nothing more. No use is shown.

label: Profiler track current frame
summary: A developer command of the game's profiler; going by its name, it makes the profiler follow the current frame.
details: The game documents nothing more. No use is shown.

label: Profiler write frame CSV
summary: A developer command of the game's profiler; going by its name, it writes the frame data to a CSV file.
details: The game documents nothing more. No use is shown.

label: Profiler is recording
summary: A developer function of the game's profiler; going by its name, it tells whether the profiler is recording.
details: It returns yes or no. No use is shown.

label: Profiler select thread
summary: A developer command of the game's profiler; going by its name, it selects a thread to look at.
details: The game documents nothing more. No use is shown.

label: Profiler set frame
summary: A developer command of the game's profiler; going by its name, it sets which frame is shown.
details: The game documents nothing more. No use is shown.

label: Toggle profiler recording
summary: A developer command of the game's profiler; going by its name, it starts or stops recording.
details: The game documents nothing more. No use is shown.

label: Pin situation
summary: Builds a command about the pin state of a situation in the situation list.
details: Vanilla wraps it in `PostCommand(...)` in the situation list window, with the situation and the word 'visible' or 'hidden'. Its return type is Command, so it only builds the command. That 'visible' pins and 'hidden' unpins is the name's meaning, not documented.

label: Pin struggle
summary: Builds a command about the pin state of a struggle in the situation list.
details: Vanilla wraps it in `PostCommand(...)` in the situation list window, with the struggle and the word 'visible' or 'hidden'. Its return type is Command, so it only builds the command. That 'visible' pins and 'hidden' unpins is the name's meaning, not documented.

label: Can pick activity phase
summary: Whether the player can pick another phase of this kind, at the given province, while planning an activity.
details: It is true when the player can pick that phase at that location (with the selected special option) and the planner still allows more phases of that type. Vanilla uses it as `enabled` in the activity planner and in the tournament contest selection.

fields.name: Location
fields.text: The province where the phase would take place.

label: Play sound
summary: Plays a sound effect event.
details: Vanilla uses it in `onclick` with a sound path built from text, e.g. a lifestyle sound named after the lifestyle's key.

label: Player can disband all
summary: Whether the player can use the 'disband all' action.
details: Vanilla uses it as `enabled` in the HUD and the military window. What exactly gets disbanded comes from the name only.

label: Can raise barter rally point
summary: Going by its name, whether the player can raise any barter rally point.
details: Vanilla uses it as `enabled` of a widget in the military window.

label: Can raise men-at-arms rally point
summary: Going by its name, whether the player can raise any men-at-arms rally point.
details: Vanilla uses it as `enabled` of a widget in the military window.

label: Can raise raiders rally point
summary: Going by its name, whether the player can raise any raider rally point.
details: Vanilla uses it as `enabled` of a widget in the military window.

label: Can raise any rally point
summary: Going by its name, whether the player can raise any rally point.
details: Vanilla uses it as `enabled` in the HUD and the military window (and in a commented-out `visible` line next to a war check).

label: Disband all
summary: The 'disband all' action of the player; going by its name, it disbands their raised troops.
details: Vanilla uses it as `onclick` in the HUD and the military window. The meaning rests on the name and those uses.

label: Is multiplayer host
summary: Whether the current player is the host of the multiplayer game.
details: Vanilla uses it together with a preparation-lobby check as `visible` in the multiplayer types file.

label: Raise all barter regiments
summary: Raises all of the player's barter regiments.
details: Vanilla uses it as `onclick` in the military window. Going by the name and that use.

label: Raise barter regiments at location
summary: Raises the player's barter regiments at a rally location.
details: Vanilla uses it as `onrightclick` in the military window, next to the left-click version without a location. Going by the name and that use.

label: Raise all men-at-arms
summary: Raises all of the player's men-at-arms regiments.
details: Vanilla uses it as `onclick` in the military window. Going by the name and that use.

label: Raise men-at-arms at location
summary: Raises the player's men-at-arms regiments at a rally location.
details: Vanilla uses it as `onrightclick` in the military window. Going by the name and that use.

label: Raise all raiders
summary: Raises all of the player's raid regiments.
details: Vanilla uses it as `onclick` in the military window. Going by the name and that use.

label: Raise raiders at location
summary: Raises the player's raid regiments at a rally location.
details: Vanilla uses it as `onrightclick` in the military window. Going by the name and that use.

label: Raise all regiments
summary: Raises all of the player's regiments.
details: Vanilla uses it as `onclick` of the raise-all buttons in the HUD and military window. Going by the name and those uses.

label: Raise regiments at location
summary: Raises the player's regiments at a rally location.
details: Vanilla uses it as `onrightclick` of the raise-all buttons in the HUD and military window. Going by the name and those uses.

label: Should show disband all
summary: Whether the 'disband all' control should be shown to the player.
details: Vanilla uses it as `visible` in the HUD, so it decides if a widget is shown. Going by the name and that use.

label: Send command
summary: Sends a game command, built by another function, to the game.
details: Vanilla wraps other commands in it in `onclick` and `onrightclick`, e.g. `PostCommand( PinSituation( ... ) )` or a scheme click on the HUD. The meaning rests on the name and these uses.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a command, e.g. the result of `PinSituation(...)`

label: Preselect decision option
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, preselects an option of a decision.
details: Vanilla uses it in `onclick` in the silk road, situation sub-region and dynastic cycle windows, passing a key: a title's key or the key of a participant group's type.

label: Has provincial laws
summary: Whether the character has provincial laws.
details: It is true when the character's government is the administrative or the celestial type. Vanilla uses it as `visible` in the realm window.

label: Recipient
summary: The character on the receiving side of what a game text describes.
details: Vanilla pairs it with ACTOR, the acting side: "[ACTOR] married [RECIPIENT]". It is also used in an interaction text about title tiers.

label: Regiment
summary: The men-at-arms regiment a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it, for example, when a regiment is destroyed or is already stationed in a place.

label: Relation
summary: Gives a scripted relation; the game documents only the return type.
details: Going by its name and return type, it stands for a scripted relation. No use is shown.

label: Religion
summary: Gives a religion; the game documents only the return type.
details: The only use shown is in the text 'Your faith is not part of $RELIGION|V$', where the name is a text variable, so what the function returns in other places is not shown.

label: Religion family
summary: The religion family a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's condition texts use it: "[religion] is [family]" and its negation.

label: Right artifact
summary: Gives an artifact; going by its name, the 'right' one of a pair. The game documents only the return type.
details: Going by its name and the sibling `RIGHT_CHARACTER`, it is the right-hand participant of a message. No use is shown.

label: Right character
summary: Gives the second of the two characters a message is about (the first is `LEFT_CHARACTER`).
details: Vanilla uses it in the game's messages. In the diarchy messages the left character is the ruler and the right one the person they share power with; in the marriage message the right one is the other spouse.

label: Message doctrine
summary: The doctrine a notification message is about.
details: Vanilla's one use is the message that a doctrine was learned, naming it for the player's faith. Messages call their second object "right" (see LEFT_TITLE and RIGHT_TITLE).

label: Right faith
summary: Gives a faith; going by its name, the 'right' one of a pair. The game documents only the return type.
details: Going by its name and `RIGHT_CHARACTER`. No use is shown.

label: Right rite
summary: Gives a rite; going by its name, the 'right' one of a pair. The game documents only the return type.
details: Going by its name and `RIGHT_CHARACTER`. No use is shown.

label: Message tenet
summary: The tenet a notification message is about.
details: Vanilla's messages use it for a tenet learned, or a tenet adopted or given up as a personal tenet, named for the player's rite.

label: Second message title
summary: A title a notification message is about, the second when it names two.
details: Vanilla uses it for the title raided in the message after a raid, and as the second title whose province an epidemic spread to, after LEFT_TITLE.

label: Rite
summary: The rite a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it, for example, as the rite a character converts to, and in the condition text "[character]'s rite is ...".

label: Rite type
summary: The kind of rite a game text is about, such as the model for a newly founded rite.
details: Vanilla's effect texts say a new rite is founded "after the principles of" this type.

label: Root
summary: Going by its name, the scope a script started with, as a text sees it.
details: The game documents it only as a script scope. Vanilla uses it in over 20,000 lines, mostly in event texts, and reaches a character from it with `ROOT.Char`, as in `[ROOT.Char.GetFaith.HighGodName]`.

label: Raise holy order
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, raises a holy order's troops.
details: It takes one argument. No use is shown.

label: Raise mercenary company
summary: A GUI command that raises a mercenary company.
details: Vanilla uses it in `onclick` in the hired troops window, passing the mercenary company itself.

label: Refresh illustration
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, refreshes the illustration.
details: Vanilla uses it in `onclick` on the main menu screen. The meaning rests on the name and that use.

label: Is release build
summary: Whether the game runs as a release build rather than a development build.
details: Vanilla uses it as `visible`: on the loading screen a widget is shown when it is true, and in the multiplayer lobby a widget is shown when it is false (and the pause menu is not shown). The meaning rests on the name and these uses.

label: Remaining timer time
summary: The time left on a timer variable of the player, in days, months or years.
details: The timer is a variable set on the player. Vanilla uses it in texts, e.g. to tell how long a coronation oath still lasts.

fields.name: SetVariable
fields.text: The name of the timer variable.

label: Repeated item
summary: Gives a list of repeated items for a GUI list; the game lists its return type as unregistered.
details: Vanilla uses it once, as `datamodel` in the faith window, with a count written like '(int32)3'. Going by that single use and the name, it makes a list widget repeat that many times.

label: Return to menu
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, leaves the game and goes back to the main menu.
details: Vanilla uses it in `onclick` in the multiplayer lobby.

label: Byte to text
summary: Turns a small signed whole number (a byte) into text.
details: Going by its name and return type (text). No use is shown.

label: Scheme
summary: The scheme a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in over 130 lines, for example to name the scheme's owner and what the scheme aims to do when it ends.

label: Saved scopes
summary: The top scope of the running script, from which saved scopes can be reached in texts.
details: The game documents it only as 'Script Scope' with the return type TopScope. Vanilla uses it in localization to read a saved scope by name, e.g. `SCOPE.sC('generous_courtier')`.

label: Secondary actor
summary: A second character on the acting side of what a message describes.
details: Vanilla's one use is the message that an alliance ended because [secondary actor] and [secondary recipient] are no longer married or betrothed.

label: Secondary recipient
summary: A second character on the receiving side of what a message describes.
details: Vanilla's one use is the message that an alliance ended because [secondary actor] and [secondary recipient] are no longer married or betrothed.

label: Secret
summary: The secret a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it for a secret someone learns: "Learns of [target]'s [secret] Secret".

label: Siege
summary: The siege a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's siege window uses it for the number of soldiers on each side: the besieging army and the garrison.

label: Situation
summary: The situation (a medium to long term affair in a geographical region that moves through phases) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it, for example when the situation moves to a new phase.

label: Situation catalyst
summary: The kind of situation catalyst a condition text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in the condition text that a situation is (or is not) affected by this catalyst.

label: Participant group
summary: The group of participants in a situation (such as a movement) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it, for example, for a movement that becomes favored or that a character comes to lead.

label: Situation phase
summary: The kind of situation phase a game text names.
details: Vanilla uses it for phase names, for example "Silk Road [phase]".

label: Situation sub-region
summary: The part of a situation's area that a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it as the sub-region that a geographical region is added to.

label: Situation type
summary: The kind of situation a condition text checks for.
details: Vanilla uses it in "The situation is ..." and its negation.

label: Struggle
summary: The struggle (a long-term conflict over a large region) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it, for example when it moves to a new phase or a catalyst is activated.

label: Struggle type
summary: The kind of struggle a condition text checks for.
details: Vanilla uses it in "Type of [struggle] is ..." and its negation.

label: Scale to fit inside
summary: Gives the scale at which an element of a given size fits inside the widget.
details: Vanilla uses it as `scale` on the bookmark screen and the main menu screen with the size '(int32)1920', '(int32)1080'. Going by the name, the scale makes an element of that size fit inside the widget. The meaning rests on the name and these uses.

label: Scale to cover
summary: Gives the scale at which an element of a given size covers the whole widget.
details: Vanilla uses it as `scale` in the in-game menu with the size 1920 by 1080. Going by the name, the scale makes an element of that size cover the whole widget. The meaning rests on the name and that use.

label: Scheme has enough advantages
summary: Whether a scheme has enough advantages to possibly be executed.
details: It is true when the scheme's agent charges reach the threshold from the script value `multi_ending_scheme_charge_to_advance_threshold_t1_value`. Vanilla uses it as `visible` in the intrigue window.

label: Select enum by text
summary: A GUI command that sets a setting to the enum value named by a text.
details: The game documents it as 'Settings - Select enum by string input'. Vanilla uses it on setting buttons with the entry's enum string and the setting.

label: Select frame by variable
summary: Gives frame 2 if the named GUI variable exists, otherwise frame 1.
details: It is used to pick the picture frame of a widget. Vanilla uses it as `frame` in the epidemics window.

fields.name: Variable
fields.text: The name of the GUI variable.

label: Choose text
summary: Gives one of two texts depending on a condition.
details: If the condition is true it gives the first text, otherwise the second. Vanilla uses it a lot in localization, e.g. choosing a building description depending on whether a DLC feature is on.

label: Choose decimal
summary: Gives one of two fixed-point numbers depending on a condition.
details: The first number if the condition is true, otherwise the second. Vanilla uses it as an argument in holy site effect descriptions and as a `value` in the ledger (100 at merit level 9, otherwise the progress toward the next merit level).

label: Choose text value
summary: Gives one of two text strings depending on a condition.
details: The first if the condition is true, otherwise the second. Vanilla uses it in texts, e.g. `Select_CString( CHARACTER.IsFemale, 'woman', 'man' )`.

label: Choose 2D position
summary: Gives one of two 2D decimal vectors (positions or sizes) depending on a condition.
details: The first if the condition is true, otherwise the second. Vanilla uses it as `position`, with values like '(CVector2f)-250,0'.

label: Choose 2D integer vector
summary: Gives one of two 2D whole-number vectors depending on a condition.
details: Going by its name and its siblings `Select_CVector2f` and `Select_float`. No use is shown.

label: Choose 3D vector
summary: Gives one of two 3D decimal vectors depending on a condition.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. No use is shown.

label: Choose 3D integer vector
summary: Gives one of two 3D whole-number vectors depending on a condition.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. No use is shown.

label: Choose 4D vector
summary: One of two four-number values, picked by a condition.
details: The engine's GUI animation editor uses it to set a tint colour: the first value when the condition is true, the second when it is false. Vanilla writes the values as text like `'(CVector4f)0.55,0.55,0.8,0.2'`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: yes or no, such as a GUI function that returns true or false

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The value when the condition is true.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The value when the condition is false.

label: Choose 4D integer vector
summary: Gives one of two 4D whole-number vectors depending on a condition.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. No use is shown.

label: Choose decimal number
summary: Gives one of two decimal numbers depending on a condition.
details: The first if the condition is true, otherwise the second. Vanilla uses it e.g. for `alpha` (transparency): `Select_float( Dlc.IsEnabled, '(float)1.0', '(float)0.5' )`.

label: Choose 16-bit number
summary: Gives one of two 16-bit whole numbers depending on a condition.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. No use is shown.

label: Choose whole number
summary: Gives one of two whole numbers depending on a condition.
details: The first if the condition is true, otherwise the second. Vanilla uses it in the tournament result texts, to pick the number of guests of one of two teams.

label: Choose 8-bit number
summary: Gives one of two 8-bit whole numbers depending on a condition.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. No use is shown.

label: Choose unsigned 16-bit number
summary: Gives one of two unsigned 16-bit whole numbers depending on a condition.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. No use is shown.

label: Choose unsigned 32-bit number
summary: Gives one of two unsigned 32-bit whole numbers depending on a condition.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. No use is shown.

label: Choose unsigned 8-bit number
summary: Gives one of two unsigned 8-bit whole numbers depending on a condition.
details: Going by its name and its siblings. No use is shown.

label: Set admin vassal candidate
summary: A GUI command that sets which character the administration window shows details for.
details: Vanilla uses it in `onclick` in the government administration window, passing the character. Going by the name and that use.

label: Camera restrictions
summary: Switches the map editor's camera restrictions on or off.
details: The engine's map editor buttons call it with the opposite of the current setting, so a click toggles the restrictions. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: yes or no; vanilla passes Not(IsCameraRestrictionsEnabled)

label: Set contest info tab
summary: Sets which tab the contest information of the activity window shows.
details: It stores the given value in the GUI variable `activity_contest_info_tab`. Vanilla uses it in tournament buttons with the value 'overview'.

label: Set game speed
summary: A GUI command that sets the game speed.
details: Vanilla uses it in `onclick` in the HUD with values like '(int32)0' and '(int32)1'. Going by the name and those uses.

label: Set Ironman
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, switches Ironman mode on or off.
details: Vanilla uses it in `onclick` on the bookmark screen and the game rules screen with '(bool)yes' and '(bool)no'. The meaning rests on the name and those uses.

label: Set locale view
summary: Sets which view the activity locale window shows.
details: It stores the value in the GUI variable `activity_locale_view`. Vanilla uses it with values like 'phase_information'.

label: Set map mode
summary: A GUI command that switches the map to another map mode.
details: Vanilla uses it in the HUD with names like 'players' and 'dejure_duchies'. Going by the name and those uses.

label: Set or toggle locale view
summary: Sets the activity locale view to the given value, or toggles it.
details: It works on the GUI variable `activity_locale_view`. The game says only 'sets or toggles'; the exact toggle behaviour is not documented. Vanilla uses it for the 'my_knights_window' button in the tournament.

label: Random observer character
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, picks a random playable character for an observer.
details: Vanilla uses it in `onclick` in the multiplayer lobby.

label: Short number to text
summary: Turns a short whole number into text.
details: Going by its name and return type. No use is shown.

label: Limit age of dead portraits
summary: Whether the portraits of dead characters should be limited in age.
details: Vanilla uses it for the `down` state of a button in the dynasty tree window. Going by the name and that use.

label: Prompt for ruler designer
summary: Whether the game should offer the ruler designer.
details: Vanilla uses it as `visible` on the bookmark screen. Going by the name and that use.

label: Show animation info
summary: Going by its name, whether animation information should be shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as `visible` in the shared tooltip file. Going by the name and that use.

label: Show character debug info
summary: Whether character debug information should be shown.
details: Going by its name. No use is shown.

label: Show character tooltips
summary: Whether character tooltips should be shown.
details: Going by its name. No use is shown.

label: Segmented control for setting
summary: Whether a setting should be shown as a segmented control (a row of choice buttons) rather than another widget.
details: Vanilla uses it as `visible`, and its negation, in the settings types file to choose between two widgets. Going by the name and those uses.

label: Stylize dead portrait
summary: Whether the portrait of a character should be drawn in the dead style.
details: Vanilla uses it as `visible` (and its negation) in the shared portraits file to switch between the normal and the dead look. Going by the name and those uses.

label: Show appoint court position
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, opens the window for appointing someone to a court position.
details: It takes two arguments, by comparison with its siblings a character and a court position. No use is shown.

label: Appoint court position if empty
summary: A GUI command that opens the appointment window for a court position, if nobody holds it yet.
details: Vanilla uses it in the inventory window with the character's ID and 'antiquarian_court_position'. Going by the name and that use.

label: Appoint or replace court position
summary: A GUI command that opens the window to appoint someone to a court position, or replace the one holding it.
details: Vanilla uses it in `onclick` in the great steppe and travel planner windows with a character's ID and a court position key. Going by the name and those uses.

label: Show court positions
summary: A GUI command that, going by its name, shows the court positions.
details: It takes one argument, presumably a character. No use is shown.

label: Detailed barter map icons
summary: Whether the map shows detailed icons for barter.
details: Vanilla uses it as `visible` (negated, together with a check whether the province has barter) in the map icon layer, and as `checked` of a map mode checkbox. Going by the name and those uses.

label: Detailed raid map icons
summary: Whether the map shows detailed icons for raids.
details: Vanilla uses it as `visible` (negated, together with a check whether the province has a raid) in the map icon layer, and as `checked` of a map mode checkbox. Going by the name and those uses.

label: Show epidemic map graphics
summary: Whether the map draws the epidemic graphics.
details: Vanilla uses it as `checked` of a map mode checkbox. Going by the name and that use.

label: Show legend map graphics
summary: Whether the map draws the legend graphics.
details: Vanilla uses it as `checked` of a map mode checkbox. Going by the name and that use.

label: Is showing succession
summary: Whether the succession screen is being shown.
details: Going by its name. No use is shown.

label: Single player, paused succession
summary: Whether a single-player game shows the succession screen while paused.
details: Going by its name. No use is shown.

label: Single player, succession
summary: Whether a single-player game shows the succession screen.
details: Going by its name. No use is shown.

label: Can log in
summary: Going by its name, whether the player can log in to a Paradox account right now.
details: Its one use enables a part of the engine's account status widget. The game documents nothing more.

label: Login status text
summary: Going by its name, the Paradox account login status as text.
details: Its one use shows it as the text of the engine's account status widget. The game documents nothing more.

label: Masked email
summary: Gives the account's email address with part of it hidden.
details: Vanilla shows it as the `text` of the login window. The 'masked' part comes from the name.

label: Account user name
summary: Gives the user name of the logged-in Paradox account.
details: Vanilla shows it as the `text` of the login window.

label: Account is connected
summary: Whether the Paradox account is connected.
details: Vanilla uses it as `checked` of a checkbox in the login window. Going by the name and that use.

label: Is logged in
summary: Whether the player is logged in to the Paradox account.
details: Vanilla uses it as `visible` in the login window and the main menu, to show a logged-in or logged-out view.

label: Is logging in
summary: Whether the login to the Paradox account is in progress.
details: Vanilla uses it as `visible` in the login window.

label: Is offline
summary: Whether the Paradox account service is offline.
details: Going by its name. No use is shown.

label: Is support-connected account
summary: Whether the account is a support-connected account.
details: Vanilla uses it together with a logged-in check as `visible` in the login window. The exact meaning rests on the name.

label: User name is empty
summary: Whether the account's user name is empty.
details: Vanilla uses it with the logged-in check as `visible` on the main menu, to show different content when there is no name.

label: Text is empty
summary: Whether a text is empty.
details: Vanilla uses it in localization, e.g. inside `SelectLocalization` or `AddLocalizationIf`, to add a sentence only when a text has content.
